_comment: Which US trail organizations exist, where their geometry actually lives, and whether OurHike may ship it (#1543). One row per organization from the maintainer's research pass of 2026-09-17. THIS FILE DECIDES NOTHING ON ITS OWN - it is the reviewed input a sources.json entry is written from, and `load` is the column a reviewer is actually reviewing. See features/ORG_BULK_LOAD.md for what each verdict costs and why the batches are grouped the way they are.

_load_values.ship: Open terms and a usable endpoint. Becomes a sources.json row that reaches hikers.
_load_values.hold: Recorded, reaches_hikers false. Either no endpoint exists or nobody has read the terms.
_load_values.via: No entry of its own - the geometry arrives through the row named in `via`.
_load_values.refuse: The organization states commercial, app-only or waiver-gated terms.
_load_values.none: No trail geometry exists to load, now or later.

_confidence_values.verified: The research pass confirmed this URL resolving on 2026-09-17.
_confidence_values.inferred: The data path is well-supported but the exact service URL was not opened. NOT A TESTED ENDPOINT.

_source: Maintainer-supplied research pass, 2026-09-17, covering 165 organizations. Mileage figures are approximate and drawn from organization, agency and Wikipedia summaries - use them for filtering, never for reporting. The three the research confirmed are USFS (>165,000), ATC (2,197.9, official 2026) and COTREX (45,076 across 236 land managers).
_attribution_obligation: The trail-name crosswalk this research used is derived from LongTrailsWiki (the OpenLongTrails project), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. That obligation attaches to the trail-name column specifically and is independent of the licence on any geometry. No crosswalk column is carried into this file, so nothing here inherits share-alike - recorded because re-adding one would.
_row_count: 163 rows from a research pass that numbered 165. Two organizations were listed twice in the source and are one row each here, per CONTRIBUTING.md's one-home rule: Rails-to-Trails Conservancy appeared as both the umbrella and its TrailLink product, and American Trails as both the umbrella and its National Recreation Trails directory. The Appalachian Mountain Club IS carried twice, deliberately - `amc` is its New England National Scenic Trail and White Mountains role, `amc-at` its A.T. maintaining-club role, and the two resolve to different upstreams.

orgs.why: Already registered and already shipping. Carried here so the catalogue's federal tier is complete, and because #1231 makes this the row that proves a nationwide layer needs a corridor clip before a second one joins it.

orgs.trails: Trails in NPS units; NST and NHT alignments
orgs.why: The single highest-leverage row in the catalogue. 21 National Historic Trail stewards and 2 National Scenic Trails hold no data of their own and point here, so one registration answers 23 organizations.
GTLF layer 7 is trails managed for public use. Nationwide like USFS, so it inherits #1231's clip requirement.
Public domain and blocked on nothing but an endpoint: the research found no authoritative national refuge-trail centerline. Held for want of a URL, not for want of a licence.
RIDB carries facilities, not trail centerlines. Recorded so the next person does not re-run this search; nothing here draws a trail.

The downloader is a human UI rather than a service, so there is no marker to poll and no URL to fetch on a schedule. USGS is already in the registry as a watched-only 3DHP row; this is a second USGS product and needs its own service URL before it can be more than a note.

45,076 miles from 236 land managers, which is the whole Colorado nonprofit tier arriving as one row - Colorado Trail Foundation, Colorado Mountain Club and the Fourteeners Initiative all reach the public through it, and the Colorado Trail itself is 159 features in it. 96,897 trail features in total, counted live 2026-09-17. Probed live 2026-09-17 by this repository, not by the research pass. THE ENDPOINT IS NOW THE QUERYABLE LAYER rather than the Hub dataset page the research recorded, which nothing could have fetched. 96,897 features is also a download-budget number rather than a detail - see #1231.

orgs.attribution: Washington State Recreation and Conservation Office
orgs.why: RCO states its data may not be copyrighted. Washington Trails Association and The Mountaineers both defer to it rather than publishing, so this row answers three organizations.

orgs.org: Utah UGRC — SGID Trails and Pathways
orgs.why: 47,986 features, with PrimaryName, OwnerSteward, DesignatedUses and HikeDifficulty. Counted live 2026-09-17 by this repository. Carries the Bonneville Shoreline Trail (281 features), the Uinta Highline (29) and the Wasatch Mountain Club's ground (40). THE ENDPOINT IS NOW THE QUERYABLE LAYER rather than the Hub dataset page the research recorded, which nothing could have fetched.

orgs.trails: New Jersey trails including A.T. segments
orgs.why: NJDEP is already a registered provider; this is a different NJGIN layer, the statewide Parks and Forests Trail System. Receives NYNJTC and State Park Service data, so it overlaps a source already fetched — POI_DEDUPLICATION.md's problem, not a reason to skip it.

orgs.org: NY State Parks / NYS GIS Clearinghouse
orgs.attribution: NYS Office of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation
orgs.why: OPRHP is already registered and deliberately not shipping: its four layers are marked fetched for review and the #771 spike only. This clearinghouse face of the same data must not quietly become the way that holdback is bypassed. Held until the OPRHP licence answer lands, which is one decision for both rows.

orgs.attribution: Wisconsin DNR / Ice Age Trail Alliance
orgs.why: The official layer, published by WI DNR from Ice Age Trail Alliance data on roughly a two-month cadence. Public domain via the state, which is what makes a National Scenic Trail loadable without an agreement.

orgs.trails: Arizona trails including the Arizona NST
orgs.why: Hosts the Arizona Trail Association's own authoritative Arizona NST as public-domain state data, so the trail arrives without the association having to publish anything.

orgs.org: NC Division of Parks & Recreation — NC Trails
orgs.why: The Mountains-to-Sea Trail, the state's own layer: 328 features in the `nc-mst` layer. Counted live 2026-09-17 by this repository. Recorded as blocked on a URL nobody had found; the URL exists and the row now points at it.

42 of the Superior Hiking Trail's 309 miles. The rest reaches the public through MN DNR, which the research did not locate — so this row is honest about covering a seventh of the trail, and the catalogue records the gap rather than implying the trail is loaded.
Advocacy and volunteer mobilisation; maintains no trail of its own.

orgs.org: Partnership for the National Trails System
orgs.why: Coordinates the NST and NHT nonprofits. Its members hold the data; it holds none.
Crews maintain trails on partner land. The partner holds the geometry.
Conservation corps. Same shape as the SCA — crews, not datasets.
Stock-based volunteer maintenance on other people's trails.
Advocacy. Mountain-bike geometry generally sits in Trailforks, which is restricted and is not this app's subject.
Education and ethics organisation. Maintains no trail and holds no geometry - recorded so that a future survey does not spend a search on it.
Acquires land along trails, including for the PCT. Project GIS is not a trail dataset.
Coordinates the land trusts, several of which do hold trails; the Alliance itself holds none. The member trusts are the rows worth chasing, and three of them are already here.
Race sanctioning and advocacy for trail running. Maintains no trail and publishes no geometry; the trails its races use belong to the land managers already in this file.

The National Recreation Trails directory at americantrails.org lists trail names and the agencies behind them; it publishes no centerline geometry. Useful to a researcher filling in this catalogue's 51 endpointless rows, useless to a map, so it carries no endpoint rather than a URL that would read like one.
Licensed by negotiated agreement and the basis of a commercial bike layer. A stated restriction, so the assume-open default does not reach it.

Already the registry's largest provider, shipping on the maintainer's authorisation recorded in sources.json's atc_licence block. The research's 'agreement required' is the general public's path; this project's basis is narrower and already written down. All 30 A.T. maintaining clubs resolve here.

orgs.attribution: © Pacific Crest Trail Association, CC BY 4.0
orgs.why: The cleanest row in the catalogue: a named licence an org chose, on a live FeatureServer, for a 2,650-mile National Scenic Trail. CC BY 4.0's attribution can be met by the sources screen export_sources.py already builds.

Published on an open ArcGIS Hub for public download with no stated restriction, which is the maintainer's assume-open case (2026-09-17). Attribution is carried anyway because an unstated licence is not a waiver of credit.
Jim Wolf's guidebook and paper-map organisation. Real steward of the trail's history, no dataset.

The model other orgs are adopting: a full open-data hub serving WFS, WMS and GeoJSON. 4,800 miles, the longest trail in the catalogue. Note the kind — SOURCE_REGISTRY.md flags ogc_features as the one adapter this pipeline does not have, and this is the row that would pay for it.
Publishes its own official layer and also feeds WI DNR, which redistributes it as public-domain state data. Take the DNR row: same geometry, unambiguous terms.

orgs.attribution: USDA Forest Service / Florida Trail Association
orgs.why: FTA relies on USFS Region 8 for the authoritative centerline rather than publishing its own, so the Forest Service row already carries it.
Distributed through AZGeo and USFS Region 3, both already rows here.

USFS administers the trail, so the geometry plausibly sits in EDW already; the association's own distribution is GPX and KMZ downloads rather than a service. Worth one check against the USFS row before anyone asks the association for anything.

Worth one email asking for a stable URL.
